protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to control input management configuration.
The intent is to allow special clients like desktop shells to configure input devices.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental, and backward-incompatible changes may be made. Backward-compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward-incompatible changes are done by bumping the version number in the protocol and interface names and resetting the interface version. Once the protocol is declared stable, the 'z' prefix and the version number in the protocol and interface names are removed, and the interface version number is reset.

interface.name: ext_input_management_v1
interface.description: This interface is a manager that allows configuring input devices.

entry.name: keyboard
entry.summary: keyboard input device, such as a standard keyboard

entry.name: mouse
entry.summary: mouse input device, used for standard pointing devices

entry.name: touchpad
entry.summary: touchpad input device, commonly found on laptops

entry.name: touchscreen
entry.summary: touchscreen input device, supporting direct touch input

entry.name: tablet_tool
entry.summary: tablet tool input device, such as a stylus on a graphics tablet

entry.name: tablet_pad
entry.summary: tablet pad input device, used for additional tablet controls

entry.name: switch
entry.summary: switch input device, representing toggleable controls

entry.name: unknown
entry.description: An unspecified runtime error has occurred. The client may retry the request.

entry.name: nonexistent_object
entry.description: The specified object or resource does not exist on the server. This may occur if the object was destroyed or the identifier was invalid.

entry.name: arg_exceeds_limit
entry.description: The provided parameter value is outside the acceptable range. For example, this may include numeric limits, unsupported enum values, or buffer overflows.

entry.name: unsupported
entry.description: The requested operation or parameter is not supported by the compositor or input backend. This may be due to hardware limitations or lack of implementation.

entry.name: permission_denied
entry.description: The client does not have the required privileges to perform the requested operation. For example, this may occur when attempting to modify system input settings from an untrusted context.

entry.name: device_busy
entry.description: The input device is currently in use or locked by another client or system component, and cannot accept the requested configuration change at this time.

entry.name: invalid_state

description.summary: operation not allowed in current state

entry.description: The requested action cannot be performed in the current state of the object or protocol. The client may need to wait for a specific event or perform a prerequisite operation first.

entry.name: already_applied
entry.description: The requested operation has already been applied and cannot be performed again. This may occur when attempting to reapply a one-time configuration or state change that has already taken effect.

entry.name: disabled
entry.summary: the device is disabled

entry.name: enabled
entry.summary: the device is enabled

entry.name: on
entry.summary: turn on the state

entry.name: off
entry.summary: turn off the state

entry.name: unchanged
entry.summary: leave the state unchanged

request.name: destroy
request.description: All objects created by the manager will remain valid until their appropriate destroy request has been called.

description.summary: get a keyboard device for a sysname
get a pointer device for a sysname
get a touch device for a sysname
get a tablet pad for a sysname
get a switch device for a sysname
set keyboard repeat rate and delay

arg.name: rate
arg.summary: the rate of repeating keys in characters per second

arg.name: delay
arg.summary: delay in milliseconds before repeating starts

event.name: device_added
event.description: This event is emitted whenever a new device is added.

arg.name: state
arg.summary: current enabled state of the device

arg.name: current_seat
arg.summary: seat associated with the input device

event.name: device_removed
event.description: This event is emitted whenever a device is removed.

request.name: set_enabled

description.summary: set the enabled state of the device

request.description: Set whether the device is enabled or disabled. Changes take effect after the next apply request.

arg.name: state
arg.summary: desired enabled state of the device

description.summary: enable or disable left+right button as middle-click

request.name: set_send_events_mode

description.summary: set the send-events mode for the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. It controls whether the touchpad sends events normally, is unconditionally disabled, or is automatically disabled when an external mouse is connected to the system.
This maps to libinput's send-events configuration (libinput_device_config_send_events_set_mode).
If the device does not support this operation, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_dwt

description.summary: enable or disable disable-while-typing for the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. When enabled, the touchpad is automatically suppressed while the user is typing on a keyboard, preventing accidental cursor movement or unintended clicks.
This maps to libinput's DWT configuration (libinput_device_config_dwt_set_enabled).
If the device does not support this feature, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_scroll_method

description.summary: set the scroll method for the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. It selects how scrolling is performed: two-finger drag anywhere on the surface, single-finger drag along the right or bottom edge, or scrolling triggered by holding a designated button.
This maps to libinput's scroll method configuration (libinput_device_config_scroll_set_method).
If the device does not support the requested method, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_click_method

description.summary: set the click method for the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for clickpad devices (touchpads with a depressible surface). It selects how secondary and tertiary button clicks are emulated: by pressing in designated corner areas, or by the number of fingers contacting the surface (clickfinger).
This maps to libinput's click method configuration (libinput_device_config_click_set_method).
If the device does not support the requested method, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_tap_enabled

description.summary: enable or disable tap-to-click on the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. When enabled, a brief finger contact (tap) generates a button click event without requiring a physical press of the touchpad surface.
This maps to libinput's tap configuration (libinput_device_config_tap_set_enabled).
If the device does not support tap-to-click, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_tap_drag

description.summary: enable or disable tap-and-drag on the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. When enabled, a tap immediately followed by a held finger initiates a drag operation, allowing items to be dragged without holding a physical button.
This maps to libinput's tap-drag configuration (libinput_device_config_tap_set_drag_enabled).
If the device does not support tap-and-drag, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_tap_drag_lock

description.summary: enable or disable tap-drag lock on the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. When tap-drag lock is enabled, an ongoing tap-drag gesture is not dropped when the finger is briefly lifted. The drag continues until the finger is lifted and no new touch occurs within a timeout period.
This maps to libinput's tap-drag-lock configuration (libinput_device_config_tap_set_drag_lock_enabled).
If the device does not support this feature, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_tap_button_map

description.summary: set the tap button mapping for the touchpad

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices with tap-to-click enabled. It controls which button events are generated by one-, two-, and three-finger taps.
'lrm': 1-finger tap → left, 2-finger tap → right, 3-finger tap → middle. 'lmr': 1-finger tap → left, 2-finger tap → middle, 3-finger tap → right.
This maps to libinput's tap button map configuration (libinput_device_config_tap_set_button_map).
If the device does not support tap-to-click, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

request.name: set_blank_region

description.summary: set a blank region on the touchpad that ignores touch input

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. It defines a region on the touchpad surface where finger contact will be ignored and no pointer events will be generated. This is useful for excluding areas prone to accidental palm or thumb contact.
Passing null for the region cancels any previously set blank region, restoring full touchpad sensitivity.
If the device does not support this operation, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

arg.name: region
arg.summary: region to suppress touch input on, or null to cancel

request.name: set_edge_safe_area

description.summary: set edge safe areas on the touchpad that ignore touch input

request.description:
This request is only meaningful for touchpad devices. It defines safe areas along the four edges of the touchpad surface within which finger contact will be ignored. This is commonly used to prevent unintended cursor movement caused by thumb resting near the edges of the touchpad.
All four edge widths or heights are specified in device-native units. Setting all values to zero cancels any previously set edge safe areas.
If the device does not support this operation, a 'failed' event is sent with reason 'unsupported'.

arg.name: left_edge_width
arg.summary: width of the left edge safe area in device units

arg.name: top_edge_height
arg.summary: height of the top edge safe area in device units

arg.name: right_edge_width
arg.summary: width of the right edge safe area in device units

arg.name: bottom_edge_height
arg.summary: height of the bottom edge safe area in device units

request.name: apply

description.summary: apply configuration changes to pointer device

request.description: Asks the server to apply device changes requested.

event.name: device_name
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the device name of the pointer device changes.

event.name: failed
event.description: This event indicates that the attempted configuration change failed.

interface.name: ext_touchscreen_device_v1
interface.description: This object provides requests to configure an input touch device.

request.name: set_enabled

description.summary: set the enabled state of the device

request.description: Set whether the device is enabled or disabled. Changes take effect after the next apply request.

arg.name: state
arg.summary: desired enabled state of the device

request.name: set_map_output

description.summary: map the touch device to a specific output

request.description: This request maps the touch device to the specified output. If the output does not support this operation, a 'failed' event is sent.

request.name: set_blank_region

description.summary: set a region that does not receive touch events

request.description: This request sets a blank region on the touch device where touch events will not be registered. Passing 'null' cancels the blank region setting.

arg.name: region
arg.summary: blank region for touch panel, null cancels

request.name: set_edge_safe_area

description.summary: set safe area on the edges of the touch panel

request.description: This request sets a safe area along the four sides of the touch panel. Touch events will be sent normally outside this area.

arg.name: left_edge_width
arg.summary: width of the left safe area

arg.name: top_edge_height
arg.summary: height of the top safe area

arg.name: right_edge_width
arg.summary: width of the right safe area

arg.name: bottom_edge_height
arg.summary: height of the bottom safe area

request.name: apply

description.summary: apply configuration changes to touch device

request.description: Asks the server to apply device changes requested.

event.name: device_name
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the device name of the touch device changes.

event.name: failed
event.description: This event indicates that the attempted configuration change has failed.
